title: With new export controls on critical minerals, supply concentration risks become reality
key_claim: For 19 of 20 strategic minerals China is the leading refiner (average 70% share); it holds about 91% of rare-earth separation and refining and 94% of sintered permanent magnet production, and the October 2025 controls extend licensing to parts and assemblies containing Chinese-origin rare earths.
frame_summary: Years of concentrated rare-earth and magnet supply, layered with China's October 2025 export controls, have turned a theoretical supply-concentration risk into a live vulnerability for energy, defence and semiconductor supply chains.
signals_supported: China rare-earth and magnet export controls escalate

title: Global trade update (June 2026): The shifting dynamics of critical minerals trade
key_claim: Since 2020 nearly 100 new export measures (37 licensing requirements, 31 export taxes, 29 export bans, one quota) have been introduced on critical energy transition minerals; in 2025 China accounted for 69% of rare earth mine production and 73 critical-mineral partnership agreements have been logged, 58 of them since 2022.
frame_summary: Surging demand meets highly concentrated supply, and governments are increasingly using export measures and partnership deals to secure access, risking a fragmentation of critical-minerals trade into competing blocs.

title: Special report 04/2026: Critical raw materials for the energy transition (Not a rock-solid policy)
date_evidence: The European Court of Auditors published Special Report 04/2026 on February 2, 2026, assessing EU measures to secure the supply of critical raw materials
key_claim: EU auditors judge the Critical Raw Materials Act's 2030 targets difficult to reach: of 60 strategic projects, 14 are unlikely to contribute by 2030 and three of four projects expected to start production in 2025-27 are behind schedule or unverifiable.
frame_summary: The EU's critical raw materials policy is not rock-solid: ambitions are clear but the bloc faces major obstacles in turning them into secure supply, and the 2030 benchmarks look out of reach.
signals_supported: EU CRMA delivery gap

title: Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later
key_claim: Washington's response to China's 2025 rare-earth restrictions is the most aggressive US industrial policy in modern history: billions across agencies, a $110 per kilogram price floor for MP Materials and Lynas, Project Vault and a $1.6 billion package for USA Rare Earth, yet true resilience remains years away.
frame_summary: China's rare-earth restrictions exposed a serious US vulnerability, and one year on Washington's billions in financing and partnerships have begun to respond but have not yet bought genuine supply-chain resilience.

title: Critical minerals geopolitics in 2026: risks, supply chains and global power shifts
date_evidence: 27 January 2026 ~ Expert comment ~ Written by Olena Borodyna
key_claim: The US has paired domestic equity stakes and price-support exploration with eleven-plus bilateral mineral deals while the EU's RESourceEU plan aims to mobilise up to 3 billion euros by 2029, a sum auditors and analysts judge far short of the diversification challenge.

title: Can Price Floors Fix America's Rare Earth Problem?
key_claim: Industry estimates an effective US rare-earth price guarantee would need to be 10 to 100 times current market prices, and a lithium price floor alone could cost $7.5 billion, making the federal turn to price guarantees costly and uncertain even if it boosts domestic output.
frame_summary: The US government's turn to price guarantees for critical minerals is problematic given large and uncertain costs to taxpayers, even if guarantees do raise domestic production.
signals_supported: US government equity stakes and price floors

title: Lender to Market Maker: The New U.S. Government Critical Minerals Playbook
key_claim: Washington has moved from lender to market-maker, blending long-tenor loans, direct equity (a 10% stake in USA Rare Earth in January 2026, roughly 15% in MP Materials), revived stockpiling and a January 14 2026 Section 232 proclamation directing price floors for processed-mineral trade.
frame_summary: The US government is no longer just de-risking projects but actively shaping critical-mineral markets, prices and industrial outcomes through a replicable playbook of loans, equity, offtake, stockpiles and price floors.

title: China adds 10 US firms, including rare-earth miner, to export control list
key_claim: On 22 June 2026 China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US firms, including MP Materials and USA Rare Earths, to its export-control list and barred procurement from 46 others, weeks after a May Beijing summit that was meant to extend the October truce, with analysts saying there is no real truce.
frame_summary: China retaliated against US measures by blacklisting the very rare-earth producers Washington is backing, signalling that the export-control front of the trade war stays active despite the diplomatic truce.

title: G7 Launches Action Plan as China Strengthens Grip on Critical Minerals

frame_summary: Faced with China tightening state control over minerals, the G7 launched an action plan to build standards-based markets and reduce reliance on Chinese rare earths.

title: TMC shares soar as NOAA backs seabed mining plan
key_claim: In May 2026 NOAA ruled The Metals Company's consolidated deep-seabed mining application fully compliant, advancing a 65,000 square kilometre Clarion-Clipperton Zone project toward a potential final permit by early 2027 under a January 2026 framework that merges exploration and recovery review.
frame_summary: NOAA's full-compliance ruling moves US deep-sea mining a concrete step closer to a first commercial permit, opening a contested new frontier for critical-metal supply.

title: China tightens grip on rare earths with strict enforcement rules
key_claim: A MIIT draft framework introduces administrative penalties, fines of up to five times illegal gains and possible licence revocation for Chinese rare-earth producers that breach quotas, reinforcing Beijing's control over a sector where it holds more than two-thirds of mine output and a near-monopoly on refining.
frame_summary: China is tightening domestic enforcement over its rare-earth producers to consolidate state control of a supply chain it already dominates and uses as trade leverage.
signals_supported: China rare-earth and magnet export controls escalate
verbatim_quote: A company that breaches the quota by less than 10% could receive fines of up to five times its “illegal gains”

title: Canada advocates buyers' alliance to tackle critical minerals supply concentration
key_claim: Canada's energy and mining minister argued a critical-minerals production alliance or buyers' club beats a bare price floor, noting Canada signed 30 new deals with 12 countries for C$12.6 billion and that France, the 2026 G7 host, has taken up the buyers'-club idea.
frame_summary: Canada is pressing allies to answer Chinese supply concentration with a multilateral production alliance and buyers' club rather than isolated national price floors, and France is carrying the idea into the 2026 G7.

title: Federal Push for Critical Minerals Stockpiling: 2025 in Review and Outlook for 2026
key_claim: The One Big Beautiful Act appropriated $2 billion to the National Defense Stockpile Transaction Fund, bipartisan bills propose a $2.5 billion Strategic Resilience Reserve, and the administration announced a $12 billion Project Vault stockpile financed by private investors and the Export-Import Bank.
frame_summary: Strategic stockpiling has re-emerged as a core, accelerating US policy tool for critical-mineral security, backed by billions in new appropriations and new reserve proposals.
